question: A wire loop is placed in a magnetic field that is increasing in magnitude but remains stationary. Using Fleming's Right-Hand Rule, what can be said about the induced current in the loop?

options.text: The direction of the current depends on the material of the loop
There is no induced current since the loop is stationary

solution:
The correct answer is __There is no induced current since the loop is stationary__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fleming's Right-Hand Rule__ is used to determine the direction of induced current.
 
• It states that if you stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your right hand mutually perpendicular to each other, the thumb indicates the motion of the conductor, the forefinger the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger the direction of the induced current.
 
• In this case, the wire loop is stationary, meaning there is no relative motion between the loop and the magnetic field.
 
• Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction states that a current is induced only if there is a change in magnetic flux through the loop.
 
• Since the loop remains stationary, the induced current will not occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field:**
 
 
• The area surrounding a magnet within which its magnetic force is active.
 
• A changing magnetic field can induce a current in a nearby conductor.
 
 
 
• **Faraday's Law: **
 
 
• It states that the induced electromotive force in a closed circuit is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit.
 
• The formula is E = -dΦ/dt, where E is the electromotive force, Φ is the magnetic flux, and t is time.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• It is the process of generating an electric current by changing the magnetic field around a conductor.
 
• This principle is used in devices like generators and transformers.
